exposure: interventional management of the second stage of labor (operative vaginal delivery after 30 min of pushing)
expectant management of the second stage of labor (up to 1-2 h of pushing based on parity)
outcome: maternal morbidity (severe postpartum hemorrhage, cesarean section, operative vaginal delivery, episiotomy, perineal lacerations, major maternal morbidity)
cohort: The study included all consecutive singleton term pregnancies who reached the second stage of labor between January and December 2022 at two third-level maternity hospitals.
finding: Interventional management of the second stage of labor was associated with a higher use of operative vaginal delivery and episiotomy, but a lower risk of severe postpartum hemorrhage in all patients and a lower risk of cesarean section among nulliparous women, with no observed clinical advantages for the newborn.
mod_finding: The interventional management was associated with a higher use of operative vaginal delivery and a lower risk of cesarean section among nulliparous women.
